newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close lower on institutional selling.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close lower on institutional selling.

text.p: Taiwan share prices finished lower in light trade on Thursday as institutional selling emerged to offset early gains, brokers said.
The weighted index closed 37.12 points or 0.54 percent lower at 6,859.40, off an intra-session high of 6,921.70.
Turnover was a modest T$52 billion.
The main index rose in early trade, inspired by news that Wednesday's auction prices on 10 state land parcels were unexpectedly high, suggesting a property market recovery.
But institutional investors' continued selling reversed the uptrend to hand the index a loss at the close, brokers said.
Plastics and electronics shares, which had been bought actively by institutions during previous sessions, were hit hard, falling 1.19 and 0.74 percent respectively.
Brokers said the selling could continue through yearend.
"With institutions continuing to sell stocks, there is little chance for significant gains this year," said Wang Jieh, an analyst at Foremost Investment Services.
Construction shares initially rose on the encouraging land auction news but late profit-taking eroded the gains. Ruentex Construction was down 30 cents or 1.66 percent to T$17.8.
Textile shares were higher, with Hualon Corp up 40 cents or 1.57 percent to T$25.9.
Increasing margin loans outstanding added to the overall investor caution, Foremost's Wang said.
Brokers said the market was likely to remain in a relatively narrow consolidation, with initial support for the index at 6,800 points and resistance at 7,000.
